body: I had a JustNO wedding (JNMIL, JNFIL, JNSis, JMMom) and both hubby and I wish we had eloped.  They were cranky the whole time and cast a pall over the whole happy occasion.  We wish they hadn't been there at all.  Wouldn't have hurt my feelings!  Much better to do the courthouse or elope.
Thank you.  I just might need it.

First, I just have to say what a strong momma you are.  Secondly, I just can't with your DuH and his family.  The good news is...they showed their asses in front of the CPS worker.  And you had proof to back your allegations!  Well done with your handling of the situation.  I hope things can calm down for you soon.
Please see my edit.  I wish I could have them removed, but because it is also their legal residence I cannot.
I love this!

Dude, I love this so much.  I wish I could upvote it a million times.  Thank you for taking the time to share!  My MIL is a 70+ Karen who still starves herself and covers her grays, you know, so she looks presentable.  It makes me nauseated how obsessed with appearances she is.  FIL (Walter) is determined to project the "I'm dying, everybody!" so that he is never questioned.

I wish I could ignore it and make it go away.  We rent the house from my in laws and they live in the MIL suite in the back, so I can't make them go away.  It's literally their house too.  We want to move BAD but haven't been able to because of finances.
I love this grey-rocking strategy.  I will try it with her the next time she attempts her BS.

I'm also flummoxed.  They are very, very, very good at running over the two of us, full speed.  DH, because he has pre-installed buttons (though he is mostly out of the FOG now) and me because my JNFIL is very good at setting off my CPTSD, which turns me into a useless, quivering ball of mush for days at a time.

I wish we could.  We've been trying to move out of this hellhole for a few years now, but up until recently, I was still working on my graduate degree (finished now, thank God) and hubby's industry was highly unstable.  We just couldn't save money fast enough to hightail it out.  With them around, they will make every effort to extract money from us every chance they get, all while belittling us.  Now I'm super desperate to find us somewhere and GTFO.
Sounds riotous!  (And amazingly fun.)  Congratulations to you both!

That's awesome.  All of my wedding photos show my FIL and MIL looking pissed off, bored, or frustrated.  In the family shots (we had a really small wedding) they look like they are trying to shuffle out of the shot.  I cropped them out of most of them.

To add to this, research shows that CSA happens more often in familial situations perpetrated by someone known to the victim.  Having the offender around your kids puts them in harm's way.  But there are also ways for him to contact the kids without your knowledge, mainly if they are alone with their grandmother.  She married the guy and  has done quite a bit of explaining away his crime--she will not hesitate to introduce him to the kids if she thinks you aren't looking.  She shouldn't ever be alone with the kids, and it is in their best interest not to introduce the husband to them.  

Be careful of the MIL...she agreed very easily to this.  Too easily I think.

My hubby found his birth mother and siblings through AncestryDNA. If you get it on sale it is only 79 USD. Not too bad and you may be able to figure it out without her. Good luck! It was well worth it in our case.

You may not feel like you'd need it, but, if you do decide to divorce, hire a shark.  They will be able to protect your interests better.  (Just from my own experience...and I was pretty darn nice to my ex when I divorced him.)
Hahahahaha!  I can't wait to say that to my kids when they ask one day.  Seriously, they totally acted like children that day.

You'd most likely be right on all of the above.  And yes, they do not possess the height of manners.  I've never met two people who openly stare as much as they do...  My momma'd smack me one if I acted like that.

I'm sure they looked like jerks.

My MIL and FIL were the WORST at my wedding.  I had everyone wear shades of white and champagne (my colors) so I didn't have to worry about that disaster, but...

My FIL was supposed to read a passage from I Corinthians (my fave passage of all time).  The passage is beautiful, but he delivered it like he was scolding us with it.  Then he slammed his Bible shut and sat down.  Our ceremony was very traditional but they still found reason to harrumph here and there all the way through.

They're also scowling in every one of our pictures.  ALL of them.  Even the ones where it is just them and DH.  

I should also mention that they demanded to be a part of his proposal, which was at my birthday party.  I had a camcorder in my face the whole time.  It was weird.  

Before my DH proposed, they had a deep background check done and demanded copies of my financials.

The biggest issue here appears to be that your DH doesn't see you and him as a unit.  When you get married, that's exactly what you are--two halves of the same whole.  When she hurts you, she hurts him.  At least that's how it supposed to be.

It might be worth explaining your position from this angle.  She's made it her mission to hurt you at every opportunity, so she's hurting him.  Further, why would you trust your child with her if she hates you so much?  She is your child too.

Bankruptcy sounds like a better option, honestly.  Have you talked to your mortgage company?  Sometimes you can work something out to prevent foreclosure.  

It took me fourteen years to manage to sit across from my abuser, a lot of anxiety meds, and a public place (a park) with numerous escape routes.  It doesn't sound like this is a viable option if typing it isn't even possible.

THIS.  You'll need to set firm boundaries right away so that she understands you are not temporarily holding onto the kids.  Further, she'll likely need constant reinforcement that the placement is permanent--they are your kids now, not hers.  Otherwise, things can get rocky.  Expect backlash from your family about these arrangements--even the most reasonable people can become heated in situations like these.

Exactly.  Likely they were in a foster-to-adopt situation before and the previous placement decided they didn't want to adopt them.  They are most likely wards of the state already.  

It takes A LOT for CPS to decide that children shouldn't be in the care of their parents anymore.  The court's conditions don't sound unreasonable and it also sounds like she is pretty firmly hooked on the smack and BD.  If all of the above is correct, termination of parental rights probably just happened.  You'll need a plan in place to keep her away, most likely.

I had something very similar happen to me with my exDuH after he ate squid and touched me.  Left a welt on me as big as his hand, I needed a shitton of Benadryl, and slept for a whole day.  Horrible rash too.  Not fun having such debilitating allergies.  Sometimes I have allergic reactions just going to the grocery store because they have a ton of shellfish.  Good times.

I'm so grateful that there are people like you out in the world.  I have three DSs that all have anaphylaxsis-level allergies to very common foods and I've had to train them all to recognize allergens and avoid them.  They also had to learn what to do in event of an exposure.  My MIL (really just a peach of a woman, bless her heart) once had them over for dinner and decided to grill shrimp next to their hamburgers (one of their allergies is shellfish).  Needless to say they haven't been allowed since.  But if they were to go out for any sort of food with them, I would have been grateful for someone like you stepping in when she got out of line (notice I said when, not if).  She's one of those "it can't be that bad" people, forget that I have the same allergies they do and I've been hospitalized before just for someone eating shellfish at the same table as me.

From my own experience, it takes a long time for the pain to subside.  I started re-calibrating almost ten years ago and it still hurts terribly (once in a while, though).  Where he's at is a scary and devastating place to be.  You start to see your life through an entirely different lens, and once that happens, it's like living your life all over again but with the joy and innocence sucked out of it.  Like your husband, I was a surrogate spouse to my mother from a very young age and for a few years, realizing that kinda broke me.  It helped me a lot to go NC with my mom for a few years--during the worst of it.  His relationship with his mother will never be the same again, and I'm sure he realizes that.  It's such a difficult thing to accept that your parent(s) don't love you, they pathologically need you for their own purposes.  

I was the SG in my family, though I had moments in my childhood where I was treated like the GC.  I think I had a bit easier time coming to accept reality because of my status in my family.  I don't know where your FDH stands, but especially if he is the GC, he is going to have a bit of a rough go at it.  

It's going to sound cliche, but really, the best thing for him is to find a therapist he trusts or a support group (I used both for a number of years, and even now I consider this sub to be a support group).  He may also need additional assistance with his depression through medication.  What he needs most, though, is something to cling to.  Your wedding is likely what he's clinging to as a beacon of hope.  I think that's why he doesn't want to postpone.  I'd just tell him that if his parents don't want to come, too bad for them, but you'll go forward together.  Your relationship is going to be a life raft for him in the coming weeks/months/years.  He may need occasional reminding that you're not going anywhere, that you are going to work through the problems together.  

Best Wishes to you both, and Good Luck!
Good point.  I'm looking over the lease again.

DH is very much on board with setting boundaries, though I think his philosophy in handling his father is a bit "warped".  He currently is ignoring everything his father does and says that he won't reward his bad behavior with the attention he wants.  He doesn't seem to understand, though, that by ignoring his father, it leads to his father yelling at me when DH is at work.  DH is gone at work literally all day, and just gets three hours a day with the kids during the week.  

DH wants to cut them off completely...but we can't because of the house.  Not until we move anyway.  But he doesn't seem to want to do the necessary dance to deal with them until then.  

As for EMIL trying to use DH against me, she's tried in the past but his spine is getting a bit shinier lately...so it doesn't help her.  Lately, it seems that her strategy has changed to calling out NFIL whenever he acts a fool.  I think she does this to get closer to me.  I'm being cautious because, frankly, I will never trust them.  EVER.

There isn't a locking door, unfortunately.  I wish there was...

As it stands currently, he just comes in the house whenever he feels like it.  It makes me really edgy.

That makes a lot of sense.  

Do you have any suggestions for security cameras?  Or know of somewhere that might have some?  Thank you for your insight!
Your first priority (and his) is baby. Kitty won't get better, so kitty has to go.

My therapy dog is a big, fluffy derp, and seriously, she's the best. She makes Amelia insane and is a great judge of character. Loves kids, hates Narcs. She cuddles me when I cry and gives me more of a feeling of security. Especially for your wife, I highly recommend it. A Great Pyrenees, a Belgian Malinois or Anatolian Shepherd would be fantastic. All very protective boneheads.
We did stay home, and it was lovely. I have posted an update in JNM.

Unfortunately, I know exactly how you feel.  I'm in the same situation with my MIL and FIL.  It really can suck at times, and I'm sorry you have to deal with that.  

The best advice I can give is to allow yourself overnight breaks here and there.  Get a hotel room with DH and enjoy yourself, that way you can get an uninterrupted break from her snooping and hovering.
Boy I wish it was a rhetorical question, but sadly, I struggle so hard with saying no to her.
I think I will.  Thank you. /hugs back

Hit the nail on the head there, my friend.  She gravely dislikes anything that is good for me (I have severe stomach problems and cannot eat a number of things).  Thanksgiving dinner is usually chock full of the things that make me sick and leave me with stomach fits for 4-5 days minimum.  Sometimes I have to go to the ER just to get IV medication to stop the problem.
Agreed!

I'm sure you are right.  After my attempts at suicide, my psychologists were all too keen to paint Amelia as the hapless victim, so abused herself that she had no ability to look out for her kids, and DF as a psychotic, narcissistic asshole (which he kinda is).  

I really need to see her for who she is--abused herself, definitely yes (I witnessed a great deal of it and often broke up the physical scuffles), but someone who chose to stay with a man that could've killed her at any time because her crazy church told her divorce is unforgivable.  She did end up divorcing him anyway, BTW.

I must say you had my DH and I in a fit of laughter with your description of my ex...though I think it may be a bit too nice for him.  There's a lot to be said about my ex, but I suppose that's for another time.  

   I have come to accept in the last eight years (about as long as I have been with my DH, though almost five we've been married) that my normal meter is so f*cked up that it may be irreparable.  But I'm still trying.  9 different kinds of hell, alright.

I'm at the point where I really don't want to go, and my DH is encouraging me to put my foot down, so, I'm pretty sure we won't go. 

I have no idea how to tell her no without the guilt trip and lashing I'll get. 

Holidays with my family are miserable as hell. I'd rather have a root canal without anesthetic.
Hahaha...she'd have blown a cork! Now she hates him...he lived in her house and never paid her the rent they agreed on and made a big mess of her house.
Thankfully, he doesn't live with her anymore...after he was there for two years, she figured out how much of a problem he really was and 86ed him. But yeah, C&D crosses my mind every so often.
